intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Ribbons hang from the railings. On the water, small lanterns bob in rows, each painted with a name or a wish.

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Lit or unlit, they float. That appears to be the main requirement.

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Welcome to the Moonwater Festival. Officially, the lanterns honor those who guided us home.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Unofficially, everyone enjoys making things float, and then we call it solemn.”

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “Both can be true.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Exactly. You are becoming dangerously good at this.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: A cluster of young sea-dwellers steers a string of lanterns toward her. Nerelle greets every one of them by name.

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: Then she listens to their concerns one at a time, including a long one about a crab.

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “They’re glad you’re here.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “This is my favorite part. They bring me real problems, and sometimes I can help.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “The crab is a real problem. I have met him.”

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “And the parts you don’t love?”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Those exist too. I used to accept every demand, until there was no room left to want anything.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Now I am sorting them. Duties that are mine. Duties I can share. Habits dressed up as laws.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “The third pile is the largest. The council is very attached to it.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: A lantern drifts into an eddy and turns twice. Then it points itself upstream, apparently bound for a different festival.

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “That one has more independence than half the council.”

intro.speaker: PLAYER
intro.text: “Does it get a say in where it goes?”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “Partly. Currents are real. How you travel with them is another matter.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “I want to keep serving my people. I also want to keep learning about yours.”

intro.speaker: NERELLE
intro.text: “People hear one wish and assume it cancels the other.”

intro.speaker: NARRATOR
intro.text: She turns from the lanterns to you, waiting to find out what you heard.

options.labelText: “Keep your people and keep exploring. You sort the piles, and I’ll listen to how they come out.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Oh, thank goodness. I had a twelve-page petition prepared.”

branch.speaker: PLAYER
branch.text: “I can still fill out a form, if it helps.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Do not tempt me. I know several excellent forms.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She reaches the wayward lantern with a flick of her tail and nudges it back into the channel with the others.

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “The sea is my home. And there is a part of me I am still finding out about.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “I would like anyone close to me to love the whole of that.”

options.labelText: “Couldn’t someone else do the ceremonies? Then you’d have all your time for exploring.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “Some of them, yes. This one I would not give away.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “It would. The way a boat is lighter with half of it missing.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: A young sea-dweller calls her name. She turns to answer, and the conversation ends there.

options.labelText: “Honestly, this all seems pointless. They’d manage fine without you.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “You have been here for one lantern. I have been here for all of them.”

branch.speaker: NERELLE
branch.text: “You did. Now, if you will excuse me, I am going to be pointless with my people.”

branch.speaker: NARRATOR
branch.text: She swims out among the festival-goers. Nobody in the water asks you to follow.
